Article.ArticleTitle: Morphological saliency prior-guided band-aware multi-modal disease diagnostic fusion network for vibrational spectroscopy.

Abstract.AbstractText: Multimodal vibrational spectroscopy provides a powerful biochemical probe for non-invasive clinical diagnosis. However, when mapping high-dimensional spectral features, existing deep neural networks are highly susceptible to overfitting high-variance noise, including baseline drift and amorphous broadband signals. Because underlying physicochemical constraints are rarely incorporated into representation learning, such diagnostically driven paradigms often lack prior-based interpretability, thereby limiting their reliability in complex medical decision-making. Here, we propose a Morphological Saliency Prior-guided Band-aware multimodal fusion network, termed MSPBA. In contrast to previous studies on spectral disease diagnosis that primarily emphasize multimodal fusion architectures or improvements in classification performance, our work focuses on constructing a Morphological Saliency Prior jointly defined by peak prominence, full width at half maximum and local residual fluctuations. This prior is embedded into both the model input and the early feature-extraction stage, enabling the network to preferentially attend to physically reliable spectral bands during the learning of high-dimensional serum spectral representations. By transforming spectral regions with both high response intensity and narrow peak width into prior masks, the proposed framework guides the neural network towards highly ordered core bands at the early stage of feature extraction, thereby reducing interference from complex broadband noise from a physicochemically informed perspective. In addition, we designed a lightweight band-aware synergy module to adaptively capture complementary feature associations across modalities. Validation on two clinical serum cohorts comprising more than 570 cases, collected from different hospital sources, instrument platforms and spectral dimensionalities, demonstrated that MSPBA achieved strong diagnostic performance and cross-cohort stability in both three-class thyroid tumour classification and binary thyroid dysfunction classification. Specifically, the model achieved an accuracy of 97.97% and an AUC of 0.9961 in the thyroid tumour cohort, and an accuracy of 97.62% and an AUC of 0.9938 in the thyroid dysfunction cohort. Furthermore, MSPBA enabled physically prior-matched band identification for interpretability analysis. By incorporating spectroscopic prior knowledge into the representation-learning process, this study improves the classification performance of multimodal spectral diagnostic models in complex classification tasks, while enhancing discriminative stability and feature interpretability across distinct clinical diagnostic settings.

Article.ArticleTitle: A 3D correlation spectroscopy framework for spectral feature decoupling: Enabling precise authentication and quantification of dairy cream fat adulteration.

Abstract.AbstractText: Traditional Raman spectroscopy for dairy cream fat (DCF) authentication is often severely compromised by temperature perturbations, which alter crystalline orderliness and obscure low-concentration adulteration signals. To overcome this limitation, this study establishes a novel analytical framework integrating Raman spectroscopy, three-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (3D-COS), and a custom 3D-CNN architecture.

By constructing 3D spectral data cubes under dual perturbations (temperature and concentration), 3D-COS successfully decoupled physical thermal responses from chemical structural disruptions. Spectral analysis revealed that temperature modulates the triglyceride packing conformation, altering the vibrational uniformity at 960 cm-1, whereas adulterants explicitly disrupt the crystalline network, producing distinct variations at 960 cm-1 and 1655 cm-1. To thoroughly exploit these high-dimensional features, a 3D-CNN model was developed and rigorously evaluated using sample-level dataset partitioning to prevent data leakage. The proposed 3D-CNN effectively captured the spatial-concentration coupling features, outperforming PLSR, SVR, XGBoost, 1D-CNN, and 2D-CNN baselines. Ultimately, the framework achieved 100% qualitative classification accuracy and exceptional quantitative precision (R2 > 0.99) for adulterants.

This study overcomes the analytical limitations caused by temperature fluctuations. By effectively decoding the highly discriminative coupled features across wavenumber space and concentration dimensions, the proposed 3D-COS and 3D-CNN framework provides a reliable, anti-interference, and mechanistically grounded technical solution for rapid dairy authenticity screening.

Article.ArticleTitle: New chromatographic and data evaluation approaches for the comprehensive investigation of metal-phytosiderophore-complex dynamics.

Abstract.AbstractText: Phytosiderophores (PS) are root exudates released by graminaceous plants that play a crucial role in micronutrient acquisition. This is particularly relevant for iron, but PS can also complex other transition metals in the rhizosphere, influencing their bioavailability and uptake. However, characterizing intact metal-PS complexes remains analytically challenging, and studies have largely relied on targeted approaches using a limited number of selected PS.

We developed a liquid chromatography electrospray ionization high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) workflow using a mixed-mode stationary phase to separate 2'-deoxymugineic acid, mugineic acid and 3″-epi-hydroxymugineic acid along with their Fe(III), Cu(II) and Ni(II) complexes. Complex integrity was preserved under mild gradient conditions, enabling quantification in negative ionization mode across a working range of 1 to 15 μmol L-1. In parallel, we utilized MetalPicker, a novel software tool for non-targeted detection of metal complexes in LC-HRMS data. By leveraging the distinctive isotopic distribution of transition metals, MetalPicker enables the discovery of metal-PS features in a non-targeted fashion. Validation of MetalPicker against a manufacturer software for targeted quantitative analysis yielded comparable results, demonstrating the accuracy and applicability of MetalPicker for non-targeted metal complex analysis. Our approach was applied for competitive complexation experiments in model samples, revealing a strong affinity of the PS towards Cu(II), potentially limiting iron bioavailability for plants.

Our study presents the first chromatographic method separating metal-PS complexes alongside free PS, integrated with the novel non-targeted metal-complex detection software MetalPicker. Together, these advances enable the determination of coexisting metal-PS complexes in samples, expanding analytical capabilities for studying rhizosphere metal dynamics and nutrient mobilization.

Article.ArticleTitle: Cascaded SDA-Exo III amplification with machine learning-driven multi-modal data fusion for self-powered biosensing.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pokkah boeng disease, caused by Fusarium spp., is a destructive disease that can leads to substantial sugarcane yield losses under epidemic conditions. Early detection is extremely challenging due to the absence of visible symptoms during early-stage infection. Conventional diagnostic methods rely on sophisticated instrumentation and external power sources, which fundamentally restrict their practical application in resource-limited agricultural settings. To address these limitations, we develop a smart biosensing platform that breaks through the constraints of traditional methods, enabling effective disease management and sugarcane cultivation in resource-limited environments.

We develop a smart biosensing platform that integrates biomolecular circuits, triple-modal signal transduction, and machine learning for automated standard curve construction. The core innovation lies in a cascaded nucleic acid amplification strategy, where strand displacement amplification is combined with Exo III-mediated cleavage to physically separate the signals, enabling the output of electrochemical, colorimetric, and photothermal signals. This design provides built-in cross-validation, reducing false positives and false negatives in complex matrices. The platform utilizes functional nanomaterials to enhance performance: ZIF-67/AuNPs improve electron transfer at the bioanode of a self-powered biofuel cell, while TiO2@Pt nanoparticles ensure efficient photothermal conversion. Machine learning algorithms (Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Lasso Regression, and Elastic Net) intelligently fuse multi-source data from the three detection modalities. The Elastic Net model achieves optimal performance, with feature importance analysis indicating that the photothermal mode contributes most significantly, followed by electrochemical and colorimetric signals. The platform attains excellent limits of detection: 16.92 aM for the electrochemical mode, 21.75 aM for the colorimetric mode, and 2.86 fM for the photothermal mode, alongside high stability and reproducibility.

This work integrates molecular biology, nanomaterials, and data science, bridging the entire chain from the construction of a biological detection platform to data output and intelligent data analysis, and establishes a new paradigm for intelligent biosensors capable of automatically constructing standard curves in precision agriculture.

Article.ArticleTitle: Enhanced illumination of Aflatoxin B1 by N-bromosuccinimide integrated with quantum dots: A ratiometric fluorescence strategy for sensitive detection.

Abstract.AbstractText: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is one of the most potent mycotoxins, posing serious health risks even at trace concentrations. Thus, developing rapid and in situ analytical strategies is essential for food safety monitoring. Unlike previously reported complex and costly methods, simple derivatization assay to enhance the intrinsic fluorescence of AFB1 has emerged as a highly attractive strategy for direct detection.

The reaction of AFB1 with N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) affords a highly fluorescent derivative, characterized by a distinct emission peak at 435 nm. This fluorescence intensity increases proportionally with AFB1 concentration. To enhance visual discrimination, a ratiometric fluorescent probe was designed using mercaptopropionic acid-capped cadmium telluride quantum dots (CdTe@MPA QDs) as a reference fluorophore, providing stable red emission at 660 nm. The ratiometric signal, generated from the enhanced blue emission of the AFB1 derivative and the constant red emission of CdTe@MPA QDs, enables accurate quantification over 0.5-75.0 ng mL-1 with a detection limit of 0.10 ng mL-1 within 15 min. In addition to quantitative analysis, the assay provides a vivid, concentration-dependent colorimetric transition from red to blue (via pink and purple). This distinct visual readout enables rapid, in situ screening of AFB1 in food samples.The probe exhibits good selectivity toward AFB1, and multivariate analysis using Principal Component Analysis-Linear Discriminant Analysis (PCA-LDA) further validates the robustness and discrimination capability of the proposed ratiometric platform. The practicability and applicability of the probe were successfully validated in corn and edible oil samples.

This study presents a facile derivatization method designed to enhance the fluorescence emission of AFB1, thereby enabling direct visual detection. Compared to conventional chromatographic systems utilizing Kobra Cell derivatization, the proposed approach is significantly more streamlined, rapid, and cost-effective, while maintaining highly competitive sensitivity and accuracy.

Article.ArticleTitle: Text-SpecDiffusion: A text-guided multimodal spectral diffusion model for few-shot renal cell carcinoma staging.

Abstract.AbstractText: Despite rapid progress in multimodal spectroscopy for cancer diagnosis, its practical application remains limited by the scarcity of annotated data, especially for rare cancers. The scarcity of such samples often hampers the effective training of deep neural networks. Moreover, clinical text is rarely used to guide spectroscopic data augmentation, and a unified framework for text-guided spectral augmentation is still lacking. To address these challenges, we introduce a clinical text-guided generative framework based on diffusion models for cancer spectral analysis (Text-SpecDiffusion). Specifically, we first pretrain a vector-quantized variational autoencoder on a large urinary stone spectral dataset, enabling the model to learn shared spectral priors of the urinary system and thereby reduce the domain gap under few-shot conditions. We then incorporate clinical text into spectral generation through a cross-attention mechanism to guide the formation of microscopic spectral features and preserve pathophysiological consistency. Finally, we introduce a physics-informed loss based on the relative intensities of characteristic peaks to preserve the physical fidelity of the generated spectra. Experiments on a real-world renal cell carcinoma (RCC) dataset demonstrate that, by combining explicit knowledge (physical constraints and clinical semantics) with implicit knowledge from the data distribution, the proposed method achieves high-quality spectral generation, with Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.970 and 0.935 for surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) and laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), respectively. In addition, relative to the original dataset, the generated data substantially improves few-shot RCC staging performance, increasing accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity by 34.37%, 35.62%, and 16.33%, respectively.

Article.ArticleTitle: Sequential surrogate optimization for supercritical fluid extraction - Supercritical fluid chromatography - Tandem mass spectrometry method development.

Abstract.AbstractText: Supercritical fluid extraction coupled on-line with supercritical fluid chromatography creates a powerful multidimensional analysis platform, but its adoption is limited by the resource-heavy process of method development. Article.ArticleTitle: A novel multi-strategy collaborative correction method for LIBS spectral intensity under laser energy fluctuations.

Abstract.AbstractText: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) enables real-time, multi-element quantitative analysis of metals in atmospheric particulate matter. However, laser energy fluctuations alter plasma parameters (e.g., plasma temperature). Moreover, due to differences in transition probabilities and excitation characteristics among spectral lines, such variations also lead to inconsistent intensity variation trends across different lines. This increases nonlinearity in spectral intensity relationships and degrades quantitative model performance.

This paper proposes a novel Multi-Strategy Collaborative Spectral Correction (MSCSC) method. This method took 50 mJ as the reference energy, with the laser energy varying in the range of 30-70 mJ. First, a sliding window-based peak extraction strategy was adopted to identify the internal standard line and characteristic lines. Second, for the internal standard line, a plasma temperature-based spectral correction strategy was applied to correct it to the reference energy level. Finally, the characteristic spectral lines were classified into two categories by a Pearson correlation coefficient threshold: those exhibiting an intensity variation trend consistent with that of the internal standard line, and those exhibiting an inconsistent trend. The internal standard regression method and the transfer learning method were then respectively used to achieve spectral intensity correction. Experimental results show that the relative RSD of the internal standard line decreases by around 64.4%, and characteristic line RSDs decrease by over 50%.

The PLSR model based on corrected spectra achieves R2 P above 0.93 for Cr, Cu, Ni, Na, and K. RMSEP is reduced by more than 60% and MREP is controlled within 0.17, thereby improving the quantitative analysis performance for sample elements under varying laser energies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Micro-FTIR identifies osteodifferentiation markers in heterogeneous mesenchymal stem cell populations.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are often used in bone tissue engineering. However, for optimized MSC osteogenic commitment to be achieved, a deeper understanding of the cellular molecular mechanisms underlying osteodifferentiation is required. In this paper we show that this can be provided by Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy in tandem with microscopy (micro-FTIR), a methodology which may also aid the rapid early evaluation of differentiation outcomes.

We report a micro-FTIR time-course characterization of human adipose tissue mesenchymal stem cell (hAMSCs) osteodifferentiation (for 21 days), considering different independent experiments and biological replicates to account for cell heterogeneity, under both differentiation and proliferation (control) conditions. Despite extensive spectral variability in both groups, multivariate statistical methods revealed time-dependent spectral changes and potential spectral signatures of proliferation and osteodifferentiation extension. Under proliferation alone, spectral changes reflecting helical proteins and lipids were seen up to day 14, stabilizing thereafter. Osteodifferentiating cells exhibited higher inter- and intra-replicate variability and a distinct spectral time-course trajectory. Evidence was found of both helical and β-sheet protein structures, with a relative increase of the former from day 6, although masked by increasing sample variability. Other osteo-specific changes were noted in lipid moieties and at lower wavenumbers (1030-1115 cm-1). The latter were found to relate to different degrees of hydroxyapatite maturity between and even within samples.

Specific spectral FTIR signatures have been identified as markers of the extent of hAMSC proliferation and osteodifferentiation, potentially enabling the rapid and non-invasive evaluation of hAMSCs osteodifferentiation outcome and of inter- and intra-sample variability.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comprehensive non-targeted LC×LC-HRMS lipidomics workflow with active solvent modulation for the characterization of endocrine disruptor effects in zebrafish eleutheroembryos.

Abstract.AbstractText: Lipidomics is a powerful approach for investigating lipid alterations in complex biological systems. However, conventional liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS) may be limited in non-targeted studies due to the high structural diversity and wide concentration range of lipid species. In this work, an optimized comprehensive two-dimensional liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC×LC-HRMS) workflow was developed for non-targeted lipidomics. Article.ArticleTitle: Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar.

Article.ArticleTitle: Mislabeling (label noise) - an often overlooked issue in chemometrics.

Abstract.AbstractText: In supervised learning, errors can arise in label values. This fact is well known in machine learning (ML), where it has been studied since the late 1960s, but is often ignored in chemometrics. The main reason for mislabeling is human errors when supervision is carried out by a person. It is also inevitable in cases where a continuous process is divided into stages for their subsequent supervised discrimination. Another reason is the imperfection of an instrumental method, which poorly reflects the differences between classes.

This paper pursues two goals. The first one is to introduce the concept of mislabeling in chemometrics. The second goal is to share our experience in solving mislabeling problems that arise in real-world examples. In our opinion, the most appropriate approach is the integration of the domain knowledge with the outlier detection methods, which should be based on probabilistic (soft) classifiers. This approach is used systematically and is illustrated by three cases that employ both well-established and new methods.

Mislabeling is a real problem that can occur across a variety of applications, reaching up to 20%, and in some areas, such as medicine, this rate can be even higher. There is no doubt that mislabeling deserves investigation and correction. In mission-critical fields, particularly in medicine, the cost of an error caused by mislabeled data can be significant, measured not only in financial losses but also in human lives.

Article.ArticleTitle: Quantitative analysis of heavy metals in ores by X-ray fluorescence with improved CARS and support vector regression using ACOR optimization algorithm.

Abstract.AbstractText: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry is widely applied for the quantitative determination of elemental concentrations in ores due to its rapid, non-destructive, and multi-element analytical capabilities. This process removes redundant noisy spectral information while preserving chemically relevant features. Subsequently, an ACOR-optimized support vector regression (ACOR-SVR) model is developed for quantitative analysis. In this model, key SVR hyperparameters are automatically tuned to enhance nonlinear modelling capability and improve generalization performance. The proposed ACSVR framework is evaluated on multi-element ore datasets involving Fe, Cu, Zn, and Pb. The experimental results demonstrate that ACOR-CARS provides more stable and compact feature subsets than conventional CARS, whereas ACOR-SVR consistently outperforms baseline SVR and other classical machine-learning models. High prediction accuracy is achieved for Fe, Cu, Zn, and Pb, with coefficients of determination (R2) reaching 0.9940, 0.9984, 0.9968, and 0.9995, respectively. These results confirm the effectiveness of integrating optimized variable selection with nonlinear regression modelling for XRF-based quantitative analyses. Overall, this study provides a practical and efficient strategy for high-precision elemental quantification in ores, offering strong potential for mineral exploration, resource evaluation and intelligent geochemical analysis.

Article.ArticleTitle: Measurement uncertainty evaluation from analytical validation data: Asymmetric coverage interval due to uncorrected significant bias.

Abstract.AbstractText: Reliability in analytical measurements depends on appropriate measurement uncertainty estimation. In top-down approaches, precision and recovery data obtained during analytical method validation are commonly used for this purpose. However, treating directional bias as a symmetric uncertainty component may result in unnecessarily wide intervals. This study proposes an asymmetric approach (ASYM) in which bias shifts the uncertainty interval without increasing the random uncertainty component.

A Python-based Monte Carlo algorithm was developed to evaluate coverage probability and interval width over recovery values from 40% to 120% and precision up to 30%. ASYM was compared with a conventional root-sum-of-squares symmetric approach (RSSu or SYM) and alternative uncertainty models (SUMU, SUMUmax, and Ue). Moreover, the models were additionally evaluated using real analytical validation datasets from pesticide residues by LC-MS/MS. When bias was small relative to precision, the approaches generally provided similar coverage. As bias increased, ASYM and SUMU generally maintained coverage closer to the nominal 95% level, whereas other models produced wider intervals and misstated coverage levels. Application to real analytical data supported these trends. A practical decision framework based on the bias-to-precision ratio was suggested.

This study systematically evaluates asymmetric uncertainty estimation for uncorrected bias, distinguishing directional bias from random uncertainty. ASYM avoids artificially inflated intervals, provides coverage closer to the nominal level, and supports uncertainty model selection using the bias-to-precision ratio.

Article.ArticleTitle: Conductometric process analytical technology for real-time endpoint control of graphene oxide dialysis purification.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dialysis is the standard route for purifying aqueous graphene oxide (GO) dispersions after permanganate oxidation, yet its endpoint is fixed by convention: a preset duration of one week to one month, or dialysis to constant external conductivity. Article.ArticleTitle: Simultaneous quantification of gold and silver nanoparticles in spiked buffered river surface water using fluorescence spectroscopy and U-PLS/RBL.

Abstract.AbstractText: The accelerated production and use of engineered nanoparticles in commercial products will inevitably result in their release into aquatic environments, raising concerns about potential ecological and health impacts. Distinguishing synthetic nanomaterials from naturally occurring colloids in environmental samples remains a major analytical challenge because of matrix complexity and the coexistence of multiple nanoparticle types with diverse sizes, shapes, and surface chemistries.

In this study, we present a second-order multivariate calibration strategy based on unfolded partial least squares coupled with residual bilinearization (U-PLS/RBL) for the simultaneous quantification of gold nanoparticles and silver nanoparticles in water samples. Fluorescence excitation-emission matrices were recorded using rhodamine 6G and a carbazole derivative as fluorescent probes. The quenching effects induced by the nanoparticles were used to construct quenching matrices, which were then analyzed by U-PLS/RBL. The proposed methodology achieved low detection limits in the picomolar range, high sensitivity, and excellent recovery (92-110%) in both river surface water and tap water samples, without requiring prior separation or pretreatment.

These results highlight the robustness and cost-effectiveness of U-PLS/RBL for nanoparticle analysis and demonstrate its potential as a valuable tool for environmental monitoring of engineered nanomaterials.

Article.ArticleTitle: Simultaneous dynamic spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare earth elements in acidic chloride media using response-specific multivariate calibration.

Abstract.AbstractText: Reliable spectrophotometric determination of coexisting rare-earth elements in strongly acidic chloride media remains analytically challenging because of weak 4f-4f absorption responses, severe spectral overlap, and baseline instability under dynamic measurement conditions. This study presents a dynamic absorption spectroscopic method coupled with a response-specific multi-scale peak-basis linear regression model (RS-MPBLR) for continuous in situ quantification of Nd3+ and Pr3+ in strongly acidic coexisting systems relevant to NdFeB magnet recycling. Characteristic absorption peaks, multi-scale spectral descriptors, and derivative-related features were integrated to enhance response specificity and robustness against spectral overlap, acidity-dependent background variation, and flow-induced baseline drift. Spectral analysis confirmed an approximately linear absorbance-concentration relationship within the investigated range, supporting peak-oriented linear modeling. RS-MPBLR was evaluated using leave-one-concentration-out cross-validation and benchmarked against partial least squares, principal component regression, and ridge regression, achieving lower prediction errors and more stable error distributions. Dynamic online experiments demonstrated continuous tracking of stepwise concentration changes, with R2 values above 0.97 and limits of detection of 0.07 and 0.03 g/L for Nd3+ and Pr3+, respectively. Cross-day segment-wise analysis further confirmed stable online predictions, with coefficients of variation mostly below 1-2% and σpred values within 0.015-0.040 g/L for Nd3+ and 0.006-0.021 g/L for Pr3+. This study provides a robust and sensitive spectrophotometric soft-sensing strategy for continuous rare-earth ion quantification in hydrochloric acid media. By combining response-specific modeling with reference-sample-based calibration correction, it overcomes the difficulty of long-term dynamic detection under online flowing conditions and enables reliable quantification for NdFeB magnet hydrometallurgical recycling.

Article.ArticleTitle: Exploiting temporal information in higher-order fluorescence data for enhanced pattern recognition: Application to saffron geographical authentication.

Abstract.AbstractText: Recent studies using fluorescence data have demonstrated that incorporating additional experimental modes can provide valuable discriminatory information. However, the discriminant value of higher-order data may depend not only on the information acquired, but also on how it is extracted and represented before classification. Here, an in-flow photodegradation strategy was developed to generate time-resolved EEM fluorescence data from saffron extracts. Different data structures were evaluated for saffron geographical authentication. Following PARAFAC decomposition, the resulting latent variables were used as inputs for supervised and one-class classification approaches to assess whether preserving sample-specific temporal fluorescence evolution improves pattern recognition performance.

Three data structures were evaluated: second-order/three-way, third-order/four-way, and third-order/augmented three-way. PARAFAC decomposition was performed for each structure, and the resulting scores were used as input variables for supervised and one-class classification. In supervised classification using a backpropagation neural network, all three data structures provided good discrimination among saffron geographical classes. However, differences between data representations became more pronounced when DD-SIMCA was applied. All three models achieved 100 % sensitivity for the target class, whereas the percentage of correctly rejected non-target samples increased from 68 % for the second-order/three-way data to 86 % for the third-order/four-way data and 100 % for the augmented three-way data. These results demonstrate that the improvement from higher-order data is not solely due to incorporating an additional temporal dimension, but also to how temporal information is retained in the PARAFAC score matrix and subsequently transferred to the classification model.

This study demonstrates that data representation is a critical factor when exploiting higher-order fluorescence information. Although all data structures provided good supervised discrimination, preserving sample-specific temporal evolution substantially improved one-class classification. The results highlight the importance of designing dimensionality-reduction strategies that retain system-specific information relevant to class discrimination.

Article.ArticleTitle: RPA-assisted three-channel Cas13a-Cas13b-Cas12a fluorescence architecture for three-channel viral nucleic acid detection.

Abstract.AbstractText: Multiplex nucleic-acid analysis requires orthogonal signal channels capable of resolving multiple targets without substantial cross-interference. Here, an RPA-assisted three-channel CRISPR fluorescence readout was developed by coupling the distinct collateral-cleavage activities of LwaCas13a, PsmCas13b, and LbaCas12a to FAM-, ROX-, and HEX-based reporters, respectively, for detection of Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), and an eastern/western equine encephalitis virus (EEEV/WEEV) group target. The corresponding singleplex assays showed no detectable cross-reactivity with the tested non-target viral templates and achieved operational analytical detection limits of 10 copies/μL for VEEV and TBEV and 100 copies/μL for the EEEV/WEEV group assay. Integration of the three Cas-crRNA-reporter modules into one downstream reaction enabled discrimination of single-, dual-, and three-target combinations, with an analytical detection limit of 100 copies/μL for each target in the equal-concentration three-target mixture. Reporter optimization provided balanced channel responses, while inter-day repeatability and interlaboratory reproducibility yielded coefficients of variation below 10%. In a preliminary matrix evaluation using contrived equine nasal-swab samples, plasmid-spiked samples and unspiked negative controls showed concordant classification between the CRISPR readout and RT-qPCR, indicating compatibility of the assay workflow with the tested sample matrix. The method provides a three-channel analytical architecture that consolidates three downstream CRISPR readouts into one reaction while retaining target-assigned fluorescence interpretation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Pocket-sized drug discovery: An AI-empowered smartphone platform coupled with single-atom nanozymes for on-site inhibitor screening.

Abstract.AbstractText: The point-of-care (POC) quantification of α-glucosidase (α-Glu) activity and the high-throughput screening of its inhibitors are pivotal for antidiabetic drug discovery, yet they are frequently hindered by the reliance on bulky optical instruments and unstable colorimetric systems. Herein, this work reported an integrated "pocket-sized" analytical platform synergizing an ionic liquid (IL)-regulated Co-N-C single-atom nanozyme (SAzyme) with artificial intelligence (AI)-empowered smartphone analytics. Synthesized via IL-mediated cobalt anchoring and pyrolysis, the engineered SAzyme featured an optimized coordination microenvironment that exhibits robust, H2O2-free oxidase-like activity. This catalyzed the oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), driving a highly specific target-triggered cascade: α-Glu hydrolyzes α-arbutin to yield hydroquinone, triggering a naked-eye visible "signal-off" reductive fading (limit of detection [LOD] = 0.106 U/L). Conversely, inhibitors block this cascade, preserving the blue signal to elegantly translate the inhibition into a distinct "signal-on" readout. To bridge the gap between benchtop precision and on-site deployment, a smartphone-assisted RGB chromaticity analysis was implemented, achieving a reliable instrument-free LOD of 0.645 U/L. Building upon this, a custom-built smartphone application was constructed to autonomously extract multidimensional color features. By embedding a multilayer perceptron (MLP) algorithm, the platform accurately interpreted these optical signals to predict α-Glu activity (validation R2 = 0.927). Utilizing this all-in-one system, the high-throughput POC screening of natural compounds was successfully executed, identifying ursolic acid (IC50 = 3.43 μM) and glycyrrhetinic acid (IC50 = 13.01 μM) as potent inhibitors. Ultimately, this work delivered a versatile, highly integrated approach that liberates enzymatic assays from laboratory constraints, offering a robust strategy for advanced biomedical sensing and drug discovery.

Article.ArticleTitle: Improved peak-parameter estimation in overlapping 1D NMR spectra through a joint-refinement extension of Global Spectral Deconvolution.

Abstract.AbstractText: Overlapping one-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) signals can leave coupled errors when peak parameters are refined sequentially, as in Global Spectral Deconvolution (GSD). These errors affect the allocation of signal among neighbouring components and their use in quantitative analysis.

We introduce quantitative Global Spectral Deconvolution Plus (qGSD+), a post-GSD algorithm that jointly refines interacting generalized-Lorentzian components while preserving the detected peak list. Constrained variable projection and analytic derivatives support coordinated parameter updates, with overlapping windows extending the refinement to large interacting groups. For simulated generalized-Lorentzian signals with complete GSD peak lists, qGSD+ substantially reduces errors in peak centres, widths, heights, shapes and areas compared with GSD alone. Experimental spectra from diverse samples show improved fits and reduced structured residuals. An offline Monte Carlo study assesses parameter uncertainty and shows that interval reliability is sensitive to line-shape mismatch.
qGSD+ improves the quantitative interpretation of crowded NMR spectra through more accurate estimates of the components already detected by GSD. The benefit depends on an adequate peak model.
